newsitem.title: USA: Stocks surge as interest-rate worries subside.
newsitem.headline: Stocks surge as interest-rate worries subside.

text.p: Stocks rose sharply Monday amid a growing belief that the Federal Reserve may not raise interest rates at its policy-making meeting next week.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up a solid 100.14 points at 7,269.67, which surpassed its May 6 record close of 7,225.32.
In the broader market, advances beat declines 16-7 on volume of 253 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 9.05 to 1,344.10.
"I think it's still the growing perception that the Fed is not going to raise rates," said John Church, chief investment officer at Glenmede Trust Co.

The Dow rose 98 points last week as investors took recent economic data and comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan as signs that a fresh monetary tightening may not be in the works at the May 20 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
Lower long-term rates in the Treasury market also boosted investor sentiment.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury was up 9/32, lowering its yield to 6.87 percent from 6.89 percent on Friday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Another factor cited for the strength was recent weakness in the dollar against major foreign currencies, traders said. A weaker dollar boosts income from foreign sales by U.S. multinationals.
"We're seeing some blue chips rally on the weaker dollar," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.
General Motors Corp. rose 7/8 to 58-3/4. Coca-Cola Co. gained 5/8 to 66.
The rally in stocks came ahead of a raft of economic data due out this week that will further cement investors' views on the direction of interest rates.
On Tuesday, the market will weigh April retail sales. On Wednesday the government reports on wholesale inflation data and Thursday, retail inflation numbers, both for April.
But investors did not appear overly concerned about the upcoming data.
"There's a change in thinking that we can have a high growth rate in the economy without inflation," Church said. "It's called productivity."
Shares in computer makers rose after CS First Boston named Compaq Computer Corp. as its "featured stock of the week." Compaq rose 1-1/2 to 96-3/8.
International Business Machines Corp. gained 4-1/4 to 171-3/4 and Hewlett-Packard Co. advanced 3-1/8 to 57-1/4.

Citrix Systems Inc. rose 11-7/8 to 31-1/8 after Microsoft Corp. said it had entered into a development pact with Citrix to provide Windows-based terminal support for the Microsoft Windows NT Server network operating system.
British consumer products company Grand Metropolitan rose 4-3/4 to 38-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, buoyed by its merger with drinks group Guinness Plc.
